key_insight: Loading classical data into a superconducting quantum computer has a substantial dynamic energy cost that depends on QRAM architecture, gate operation, and cryogenic attenuation.
engineering_relevance: At fixed target fidelity, optimizing operating conditions and attenuation across refrigerator stages can change average dynamic power by a factor of two or more.
method: Apply the metric-noise-resource framework to connect QRAM query fidelity and power with hardware parameters.
Analyze linear-depth multiplexer and bucket-brigade QRAM architectures, including thermal photons and gate errors.
Adapt bucket-brigade QRAM to native superconducting gates and refine fidelity estimates using the fully decomposed schedule.
evidence_signal: For a representative 12-address-qubit bucket-brigade query, the analysis yields 0.969 fidelity, 3.51×10⁻⁴ J dynamic energy, 4.38 W average dynamic power, and 64.4 W peak power.
watch_item: These are model-based dynamic-cost estimates, not a reported hardware demonstration or a complete accounting of system energy overheads.
paper_title: The energetic cost of loading classical data in quantum computers
